content.text: undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding; markedly impaired hepatic, renal or cardiac function; pregnancy; breastfeeding; active or past thrombosis or thromboembolic disease.
Do a sensitive pregnancy test right before starting and use nonhormonal contraception during therapy: in utero exposure may cause androgenic effects on a female fetus.

Thromboembolic events, including life-threatening or fatal strokes, have been reported. Long-term use: peliosis hepatis and benign hepatic adenoma, which may be silent until a life-threatening intra-abdominal hemorrhage. Several cases of benign intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri): with its symptoms, screen for papilledema and stop danazol if present.
